title: Lasers and energy-based devices in skin of colour: a 2026 clinical review of safety and settings
headline: A new JAAD review for Fitzpatrick IV-VI says low-fluence Q-switched and picosecond Nd:YAG lasers and conservative non-ablative fractional settings are the safer end, ablative modalities carry more complications, and large prospective trials in darker skin are lacking.
evidenceTier: Expert narrative review (abstract read); no pooled data
fit: Useful as a question list before a device treatment. It brings no new product or protocol, and it states the evidence in darker skin is thin.
displaces: Fits nowhere as a product; it informs which device settings to ask about.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Abstract (read): in Fitzpatrick IV-VI, higher epidermal melanin competes for light energy and raises the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, hypopigmentation, blistering and scarring.

Authors' summary: low-fluence Q-switched and picosecond Nd:YAG suit pigmentary disorders and tattoo removal; non-ablative fractional lasers are safe at conservative settings; ablative modalities have higher complication rates; strict photoprotection and sequential lower-energy sessions matter before and after.
Stated gap: large prospective trials in darker skin types and standardized parameters are lacking. Full text not opened (paywalled; not attempted).
toneData: Review of Fitzpatrick IV-VI literature; no new data
fitLine: A checklist for conversations with a clinician; adds no product to the routine.

fitAxes.why: Post-procedure barrier care is addressed in general terms in the abstract.
